Done. This question exposed a genuinely new, generalizable category.

What I learned and saved:

Skill (officeqa-treasury-bulletin) — added a new section "VISUAL chart questions: counting features on LINE PLOTS". Key procedural points for future runs:
- These are vision tasks on the Bulletin's front "Chart" pages, NOT table extraction — pdftotext is useless (no extractable peaks).
- MUST render the page at 300+ dpi via pdftoppm and use vision_analyze; crop/zoom per panel if peaks are dense.
- Count EVERY line in EVERY chart panel and SUM — the #1 error is counting one panel/line and missing others.
- Off-by-one (my 17 vs gold 18) is almost always a MISSED peak — an edge/endpoint peak or a faint/dashed secondary line — so bias toward re-scanning for one MORE rather than removing one. List peaks per line so the total is auditable.

Memory — added a compact cross-session note flagging that OfficeQA includes visual chart-counting questions with the render-and-audit method, since this is a category my prior memory didn't cover at all.

This wasn't per-question trivia — it's a recurring task structure (local maxima/minima/crossings on line plots) with a specific tooling requirement and a characteristic failure mode, so it's worth the skill + memory write.
